entities.name: Primary polydipsia
observations: Excess water intake causes hypotonic polyuria with maximally dilute urine, low-normal plasma osmolality, and mild hyponatremia from suppressed endogenous AVP.
Best explains plasma osmolality 282 mOsm/kg, sodium 135 mEq/L, urine osmolality 100 mOsm/kg, urine specific gravity 1.006, and urine volume 3.92 L/day in this case.

entities.name: Central diabetes insipidus
observations: Untreated complete central diabetes insipidus usually causes dilute urine with normal-high or elevated plasma osmolality and sodium; the patient's low-normal plasma osmolality and mild hyponatremia argue against it.

Prior pituitary surgery increases plausibility of partial central diabetes insipidus, but high water intake could mask it; confirmation would require supervised water deprivation with copeptin or desmopressin response.

entities.name: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion
observations: SIADH causes hypotonic hyponatremia with inappropriately concentrated urine, generally urine osmolality above 100 mOsm/kg and often substantially higher; urine osmolality of 100 with marked polyuria does not fit.

entities.name: Amitriptyline
observations: Amitriptyline may promote thirst or water intake through anticholinergic dry mouth, but direct medication-induced polyuria is less likely; medication-associated SIADH would not explain maximally dilute urine.
